answer: Adaptive creation-cost ramp makes each new agent identity solve a proof-of-work puzzle scaled by a public signal of recent creation. Enforcement charges 2^20 hash attempts for the next identity, doubling after 1,000 identities in a rolling hour, so bursts spread like a comet tail into higher compute bills. A periodic beacon seeds puzzle randomness; an attacker adding N identities after a cluster pays about N×2^20 hashes in electricity and hardware time, not a flat fee.
